B2-01.summary: Anonymous GET /elections/{id}/tally/draft synchronously recomputes the full homomorphic aggregate (and after restart/eviction the full proof-verifying ballot analysis) on the single event loop on every call.
B2-01.scenario: Once any election has its tally aggregate posted (TALLYING/STALLED/AUDIT/ARCHIVED/IMPORTED), an anonymous client loops GET .../tally/draft; with 2,000 counted ballots each request stalls the whole instance 5.5-6.9 s.
B2-01.evidence: PoC packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts in /home/user/audit/quietvote-b2, `node --test --test-name-pattern=B2-01 test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts`: aggregate 2.659-3.344 ms per counted ballot; 2000 counted -> 409 after 5539-6948 ms with /healthz delayed equally; analyzeBallotLog 116-119 ms per ballot (PoC injects 2,000-ballot set into cached analysis).
B2-01.suggested_fix: Serve draft from stored aggregate; return 409 before work when fewer than t shares; cache per (decrypters, shares); move work to a bounded worker queue; consider class P or coordinator-only access.

B2-02.summary: POST /imports runs full verifyElection on the event loop and checks ELECTION_EXISTS only after full verification, so a valid bundle can be resubmitted repeatedly to stall the instance.
B2-02.scenario: Attacker creates an org (default registrationMode open) and resubmits a large public bundle with new Idempotency-Keys; each submission stalls the instance for full proof verification, then fails ELECTION_EXISTS.
B2-02.evidence: PoC B2-02 in packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts: 6 ballot entries, first import stall 959-1034 ms, duplicate (refused) stall 794-1304 ms via perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay.
B2-02.suggested_fix: Check electionAny(manifest.election_id) and quota before verifyElection; verify in a worker with CPU budget; per-org import rate; correct NOTES.md:144.

B2-03.summary: instance_admin keys, once seeded, can never be revoked; removing them from adminKeys leaves them active and no API revokes them.

B2-03.evidence: PoC B2-03 in packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts: after removal GET /admin/status -> 200; POST /orgs/<org>/keys (org_owner) -> 201.
B2-03.suggested_fix: At start, revoke every instance_admin key not in adminKeys with an operator_audit row; document rotation.

I also read election.ts:897-930 (vNotice: state checks plus the maxHalts cap, default 3, config.ts:228) and records.ts:13-18,33. ControlBody is {proto,type,action,reason?}. It has no seq, nonce or state binding. There is no check that the same body bytes are already on the log. The QV-18 header author_nonce (QV-18 §5.3 step 6) only deduplicates headers, so a new header around an old body passes. No spec or ADR permits single-signer re-use. Re-pausing is limited by maxHalts. Re-resuming has no limit. Impact is on availability and governance, not on vote secrecy or the count. Invalidate/cancel/abort are terminal, so replay matters only for pause, resume and security-notice.

Compare election_open (election.ts:830), which does check voting_open. Specs: QV-03 §5.5 (docs/03-governance-and-policy.md:203) says 'No early close. Close before close_at is impossible except HALT->CANCELLED'. QV-16 §5.14.3 (docs/16-crypto-protocol.md:662) says 'the coordinator may not close early', stated as a verifier check. QV-18 threat row docs/18:473 treats early close as visible and flagged by the verifier. QV-18 §5.5 (docs/18:222) requires server_time >= closes_at only for the delegated closer key. server/NOTES.md:42-43 does not document early close as allowed. No ADR permits it, so it does not conform to QV-03. It is mitigated because the verifier fails the election when witnessed.

When witness_quorum > 0 the outcome is a verifier E_TIME_WINDOW failure, so it is a visible availability/governance abuse rather than an undetected integrity loss. With witness_quorum = 0 it is only caveated. The fix is a server-side guard (now >= voting_close - clock_skew_s), which also needs the test helpers changed: the World.close / fullElection helpers rely on early close.

B2-01.notes: packages/server/src/app.ts:410-421 registers GET /tally/draft as cls R, auth none, and calls rt.buildTallyDraft(use). buildTallyDraft (election.ts:1150-1161) calls ensureAnalysis (election.ts:1041-1058); the analysis is cached only in memory (st.analysis), so after a restart or pool eviction the first call runs analyzeBallotLog, which verifies the proofs of every ballot. It then calls protocol buildTally, which runs aggregate(p, counted) on every call (tally.ts:227) and ignores the cached st.aggs. With no shares, the 409 E_TALLY_INSUFFICIENT is only returned after the aggregate and decrypt attempt. Measured in real elections with no injected data: about 3.5-4.3 ms of extra synchronous work per counted ballot on every call, and about 132 ms per ballot on the first call after a restart. A concurrent /healthz waited for the whole call. Extrapolated to 2,000 counted ballots, that is about 7-8 s per anonymous request. The default read rate limit (config.ts:146, 120 per minute per bucket) does not stop it, because one bucket can request far more CPU time than a minute holds. This conflicts with QV-29-REQ-019 (heavy proof work in bounded workers; event-loop p99 under 100 ms). B2-02.notes: In verifyBundle, imports.ts:196 calls `await verifyElection(electionJ)`. Protocol verify.ts:91-100 run() does not yield inside its per-ballot proof loop; its only await is adjudicateDkg. All ballot proofs are therefore checked in one synchronous block. The duplicate check control.electionAny(vb.electionId) is in commitImport (imports.ts:323), which runs only after verifyBundle has finished (ext-routes.ts:107-108). The route's pre-checks (ext-routes.ts:96-103) cover org and quota but not existence. My bundle had 6 ballot entries: the duplicate import blocked the event loop for about 1.1 s in one stretch and was then refused with ELECTION_EXISTS. NOTES.md:144 says verification 'yields to the event loop', but it yields only between stages. Mitigating factors, which keep this at Medium: POST /imports is class X, and the default export limit is 2 per hour per bucket (config.ts:152). importQueueMax is 2 and maxImportUploads is 2. Jobs run one at a time. The caller needs an org key, but registrationMode defaults to 'open' (config.ts:200). The cost grows with bundle size (about 130 ms per ballot), so a large public bundle replayed twice an hour per address still stalls the whole instance for minutes. The duplicate ordering means the replay uses no election quota.

That limits the rate, so I lowered the impact assessment, but it does not remove the stall. No spec permits it: QV-29-REQ-019 requires bounded worker verification.
